questions.q:
The correct order of rates of addition of ${Br}_{2} /$water to the following alkenes is

[A]~${CH}_{2} = {CH}_{2}$

[B]~${CH}_{2} = CH - {NO}_{2}$

[C]~${CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - CH = {CH}_{2}$

[D]~${CH}_{3} - CH\mathop{CH3}_{|} = {CH}_{2}$
questions.solution:
Addition of& ${Br}_{2} /$ water to the alkene is example of electrophilic addition reaction. This reaction take place in two steps. In first step electrophile is added to the alkene and intermediate carbocation is formed. This step is also called rate determining step.~

So, reactivity of this reaction depends on stability of carbocation formed and as we know for carbocation~$3 ° > 2 ° > 1 °$. So, reactivity order will be

[B]~${CH}_{2} = CH - {NO}_{2}$~<~[A]~${CH}_{2} = {CH}_{2}$~< [C]~${CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - CH = {CH}_{2}$~<~[D]~${CH}_{3} - CH\mathop{CH3}_{|} = {CH}_{2}$

questions.q: In which of the following reactions, $t$-butyl benzene is formed 1. Benzene $+t$-butyl chloride $\stackrel{\mathrm{AlCl}_3}{\longrightarrow}$ 2. Benzene $+\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2 \stackrel{\mathrm{BF}_3}{\stackrel{\mathrm{HF}}{\longrightarrow}}$ 3. The given reactions take place as follows. 1. The replacement of H-atom in benzene, by alkyl group can be brought about alkyl chloride in presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$. Reaction is known as Friedel-Craft's alkylation reaction.

questions.q: Benzene reacts with $n$-propyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous ${AlCl}_{3}$ to give predominantly
questions.solution:
This reaction is known as Friedel Craft's alkylation reaction. in presence of anhydrous& ${AlCl}_{3}$,~n-propyl chloride introduce an alkylating agent. It is an electrophilic substitution reaction.~

Reaction occurs in following~step.

Generation of electrophile.

${CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{CH}_{2}Cl + {AlCl}_{3} \to {CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{CH2}^{+} + {AlCl4}^{-}$

Carbocation formed in step 1 rearranges to form secondary carbocation.

${CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{CH2}^{+} ↔ {CH}_{3}\overset{+}{CH}{CH}_{3}1 ° 2 °$

This secondary carbocation attack on benzene ring.

Next step is the abstraction of proton from conjugate base

Hence,& the product is isopropyl benzene.

Kolbe electrolysis of \($\mathrm{CH}}_{3} \mathrm{COO}^{-} \mathrm{Na}^{+}\). At anode,
\(\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{CH}}_{3}^*+$\mathrm{CH}}_{3}^* \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}}_{3} \underset{($\mathrm{A})}{-$\mathrm{CH}}_{3}} \\ \text{ and } 2 \mathrm{CH}}_{3}-$\mathrm{CH}}_{3}+7 \mathrm{O}}_{2} \stackrel{\left(\mathrm{CH}}_{3} \mathrm{COO}}_{2} $\mathrm{Mn}\right.}{\longrightarrow} 4 $\mathrm{CO}}_{2}+\underset{ \mathrm{(D)}}{6 \mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}} \end{aligned}\) \($\mathrm{CO}}_{2}+ \mathrm{O}}_{2} \longrightarrow \underset{\mathrm{(C)}}{\mathrm{CO}}+$\mathrm{O}}_{3}\) \(\mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{NaOH} \rightleftharpoons \underset{\text{(Salt)}}{\mathrm{HCOONa}}\) Hence, \(A\) is \(\mathrm{C}}_{2} $\mathrm{H}}_{6}\) and \(D\) is \( \mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}$\).$
